title: 1755. Closest Subsequence Sum

examples.explanation: Choose the whole array as a subsequence, with a sum of 6. This is equal to the goal, so the absolute difference is 0.
Choose the subsequence [7,-9,-2], with a sum of -4. The absolute difference is abs(-4 - (-5)) = abs(1) = 1, which is the minimum.

hints: The naive solution is to check all possible subsequences. This works in O(2^n).
Divide the array into two parts of nearly is equal size.
Consider all subsets of one part and make a list of all possible subset sums and sort this list.
Consider all subsets of the other part, and for each one, let its sum = x, do binary search to get the nearest possible value to goal - x in the first part.
